    AI Overview
    Actor and martial artist Chuck Norris
    passed away on March 20, 2026, at age 86, following a sudden hospitalization for a medical emergency on the island of Kauai, Hawaii. The legendary action star, known for "Walker, Texas Ranger," was on vacation at his Hawaii home when the incident occurred, surrounded by family, according to reports. 
    Key Details Regarding the Incident 
    • Hospitalization & Death: TMZ reports initially indicated Norris was hospitalized in Kauai, Hawaii, after a medical emergency, with news of his passing emerging shortly after.
    • Recent Activity: Just before the incident, the 86-year-old actor had celebrated his birthday on March 10, posting a video of himself training.
    • Location: The incident took place near his home on Kauai's North Shore, which he has owned since 2015.
    • Family Statement: The family requested privacy, noting that he was surrounded by loved ones at the time of his passing, say fox61.com and YouTube. 
    The specific cause of the medical emergency was not disclosed, according to WCNC and ABC10.

    AI Overview
    According to reports on March 19, 2026, 86-year-old Chuck Norris was hospitalized on Kauaʻi, Hawaii, following an undisclosed medical emergency. Despite the incident, sources indicate he is in good spirits, having been active and training on the island shortly before the emergency. No further details about his condition have been released. 
    Key Details Regarding the Incident: 
    • Location: Norris was hospitalized at Wilcox Medical Center in Lihue, Kauaʻi.
    • Nature of Emergency: The specific medical issue has not been disclosed.
    • Condition: Sources report he is in good spirits.
    • Activity: He had recently celebrated his 86th birthday on March 10, posting a video of himself training, notes AL.com. 
    This story is developing and details remain limited, says Beat of Hawaii.
